description: The group consists of a single rendered data table, captioned Table IV, "Chemical composition of alloys processed by AIMFC with a different carbon level". There are no axes, micrographs or plots; the whole image is tabular text on a white background. The header has two tiers: "Sl. no." and "Alloy" on the left, then a spanning header "Alloy composition" above five analytical columns labelled "Al (wt.%)", "Si (wt.%)", "Mn (wt.%)", "S (wt.%)", "C (wt.%)". Five data rows list the alloys Fe-7Al-.002C, Fe-7Al-0.15C, Fe-7Al-0.35C, Fe-7Al-0.5C and Fe-7Al-1.0C with Al = 6.86, 6.92, 6.78, 6.95, 7.10 wt.%; Si = 0.18, 0.17, 0.19, 0.15, 0.18 wt.%; Mn = 0.16, 0.18, 0.15, 0.12, 0.13 wt.%; S = 0.004, 0.005, 0.004, 0.004, 0.002 wt.%; and C = 0.002, 0.15, 0.35, 0.50, 1.00 wt.%. The table demonstrates that the Fe-7Al-C series is a controlled study in which carbon is varied systematically from 0.002 to 1.00 wt.% while Al, Si and Mn are held roughly constant, and that the carbon figure in each alloy designation matches its analysed carbon content; sulfur appears only at residual impurity level.

observations.observation: The image contains only text/table content: a two-tier header ('Sl. no.', 'Alloy', then spanning 'Alloy composition' over 'Al (wt.%)', 'Si (wt.%)', 'Mn (wt.%)', 'S (wt.%)', 'C (wt.%)').
Five alloys are tabulated: Fe-7Al-.002C, Fe-7Al-0.15C, Fe-7Al-0.35C, Fe-7Al-0.5C, Fe-7Al-1.0C.
Aluminium content is printed as 6.86, 6.92, 6.78, 6.95 and 7.10 wt.% for rows 1 to 5 respectively, i.e. all near the nominal 7 wt.% Al despite the different carbon levels.
Carbon content is printed as 0.002, 0.15, 0.35, 0.50 and 1.00 wt.% for rows 1 to 5, matching the carbon figure written in each alloy designation (Fe-7Al-.002C through Fe-7Al-1.0C).
Silicon ranges only between 0.15 and 0.19 wt.% and manganese between 0.12 and 0.18 wt.% across all five alloys.
Sulfur is the lowest reported element, printed as 0.004, 0.005, 0.004, 0.004 and 0.002 wt.% for rows 1 to 5, indicating a residual impurity level.
The table reports analysed compositions in wt.% only; iron is not listed as a column and is presumably the balance.
The caption states the alloys were processed by AIMFC with a different carbon level.
The carbon span from 0.002 to 1.00 wt.% at essentially constant Al level defines the fixed-comparison variable of this alloy set.
The paper abstract states the work concerns lightweight steels based on Fe-Al alloys containing 7 wt.% and 9 wt.% aluminium, so this table documents the 7 wt.% Al branch.
